title: User-defined namespaces and the scope resolution operator
recap: A user-defined namespace places related declarations in a named scope and prevents otherwise identical identifiers from colliding. Namespace definitions belong at global scope or inside another namespace.

The scope resolution operator :: selects an identifier from a particular namespace. Qualified names such as Shipping::fee make the intended declaration explicit without importing every name from that namespace.
objectives: Define functions with identical signatures in two different namespaces.
Use the scope resolution operator to select each function explicitly.
Observe how namespaces prevent a naming collision.
Avoid using directives when qualification is clearer.
warnings: A namespace definition cannot be placed inside a function body.
Do not add custom declarations to namespace std.
A declaration and its definition must use the same namespace.
challenge: Define fee(int baseCharge) in both Shipping and Billing. Shipping adds 2 to the base charge while Billing adds 5. Call each function with a base charge of 10 by using its qualified name and print both results.
hints: Place one fee definition in namespace Shipping and the other in namespace Billing.
Return baseCharge + 2 from Shipping::fee and baseCharge + 5 from Billing::fee.
Call the functions as Shipping::fee(baseCharge) and Billing::fee(baseCharge).
